## Result

- Skill: design-review
- Review status: changes-requested
- Package members: design, system and workflow at the exact stored subject identities, unchanged since design-review-r2.
- Upstream review ID: proposal-review, unchanged approved direction.
- Review ID and round: design-review-r3, independent reassessment after three new user-reported concerns.
- Material findings: des-review-f2, des-review-f3, des-review-f4.
- Correction targets: primary-agent/design; Design for f2/f3 and Design/Workflow ownership reconciliation for f4.
- Recording status: recorded through targeted v2 review/finding operations.
- Open blockers: no missing necessary direction decision or unassessable evidence; three actionable Design corrections prevent approval.
- Immediate next stage: isolated return to Route for authorized correction, without this reviewer selecting activity or editing models.
- Claim limitations: no current Design approval or planning readiness; no implementation, final Verify, adoption or publication claim.

## Assessment and prior evidence

The new user concerns are independently substantiated by current Design/Workflow and retained installer/resource contracts. The package still has the previously assessed sound overall direction, component/system boundaries, source/ADR scope, Test/Review and Closeout separation, representative local/integrated intent and bounded follow-up ownership. The original des-review-f1 example-preservation correction remains resolved and is not reopened. However, the newly inspected managed-tree path contradicts the prior compatibility sufficiency conclusion; the explicit resource decomposition and retained Workflow row also leave material gaps. Required corrections have safe author-owned outcomes within the accepted direction, so changes-requested is the ordered judgment.

The previous r2 subjects and body are preserved. Its applicability is restricted to stale because material new evidence defeats reliance even without changed model hashes, under RC-SR-05/06. The current whole-package judgment is r3; recording it does not erase the prior missed concerns or retarget old findings.

## Finding des-review-f2

Material; artifact-local, design; owning stage design. Location: Design Public invocation compatibility (operator cleanup then retry), DES-SR-17 and DES-DEC-04. The contract directs the operator to remove obsolete selected-target entrypoints and retry while preserving existing project state, drift protection and the existing installer behavior. Lockfile R46–R51 require comparing installed tree identity with the recorded tree and blocking drift by default; TNI-R19–28 protect implicated roots/state. Actual lockfileDriftBlocker in packages/rigorloop/dist/bin/rigorloop.js compares file count and tree hash; existingStateSafetyBlocker applies that to the selected root, and handleInit also applies firstLockfileDriftBlocker with --write-state. Deleting spec/architecture from an otherwise matching managed tree changes precisely that recorded basis. The proposed retry therefore reaches generated-output-drift instead of a defined upgrade. Existing special managedWorkflowMigration is explicitly for workflow-to-route and is excluded from this new guard; generic --write-state is not a stated remedy. This is an independently supported recovery/compatibility contract gap, not a claim of an executed installer bug reproduction.

Required outcome and safe resolution: Define an executable operator-authorized transition for an otherwise clean managed legacy install that assesses the original locked basis before removal and reconciles the verified replacement and selected state under an explicit installer-owner contract. Name a valid existing replacement/reinitialization path or the smallest installer-owner amendment; distinguish this from generic --write-state. Preserve unrelated targets, roots, user changes and authorization boundaries, and specify recovery after interruption or failed replacement. Include intended outcomes for clean managed legacy, modified old entries and interrupted retry, so progress to a coherent design installation does not require silent state reset, a broad force escape or permanent old skills. Safe correction: Design author reconciles invocation policy with retained installer contracts and relevant System integrated outcomes before Delivery; no implementation is performed by this review.

## Finding des-review-f3

Material; artifact-local, design; owning stage design. Location: Design Building Block View resource table and following unnamed historical feature-format paragraph; Technical reasoning and decisions legacy scaffolds; Required consumer reconciliation template row. DES-SR-14 promises substantive unmigrated-source work under its retained format. The document expressly says the full historical feature-format resource is required for that invocation, but the selected exact resource decomposition names no such resource and does not assign the complete format procedure to legacy-source-reconciliation.md. Legacy architecture/ADR scaffolds are retained under repository templates/ with no determination whether these are contributor-only or required installed aids. Skill contract R47d/e, R48a and R49 require contained explicit packaged resources and prohibit treating repository templates/ as an implicit packaged resource class. Consequently the installed design path lacks a settled sufficient method/scaffold basis for its promised legacy amendment; internal checkout access or retired skills cannot supply that missing public dependency.

Required outcome and safe resolution: Name the required packaged historical feature-format resource and exact load condition, or explicitly assign the complete necessary legacy procedure to an already selected resource. Classify repository templates as contributor-only aids and supply any required public scaffolds inside the permitted skill-local package, or state a sufficient project-supplied scaffold contract without assuming internal checkout availability. Distinguish missing project behavioral authority from missing packaged authoring guidance. Add a representative clean installed-package invocation that substantively amends an unmigrated contract under its existing format without old skill packages, the internal checkout or forced model migration. Safe correction: the Design author settles resource responsibility and installed acceptance intent; Delivery allocates actual resources and package checks.

## Finding des-review-f4

Material; cross-artifact, design and workflow; owning stage design. Location: Workflow Adoption support surfaces and completion check, boundary method/feature authoring format/validator row: "Workflow owns the retained mapping; Delivery verifies affected consumers". In the same current model, WF-SR-07 and Model validation and proof mapping transfer the model/feature-document mapping to Design DES-SR-09/10/11/12/16/19. Design Selected replacement map likewise selects the Workflow document/proof mapping for transfer. The retained adoption row is not explicitly marked as an historical ownership statement and assigns the same mapping back to Workflow. This contradicts the intended single current owner during coordinated adoption, even though prior retirement scope itself is retained.

Required outcome and safe resolution: Make the retained adoption-support row reference Design as the mapping owner and Workflow as coordination/consumer owner, with Delivery retaining concrete consumer verification. Preserve the earlier retirement scope and source identities without leaving a second current mapping authority. Safe correction: the Design author makes the bounded Workflow ownership-reference edit and checks it against Design replacement and structural-mapping sections; no new policy or gate is needed.

## Evidence and limits

The required three-model package was completely inspected in prior assessments and remains byte-identical by fresh CLI subject inspection. This reassessment revisits the affected sections and their relevant interactions, reads the precise lockfile R46–51 and target-native state-safety constraints, actual lockfileDriftBlocker/existingStateSafetyBlocker/handleInit branches, and skill-contract R47–54. No customer files, installed roots, archived package, engine or model content was changed. The installer result is a source/contract counterexample; no end-to-end execution or measured failure is claimed. No new tests or adapter generation were run for this assessment. Record validation and git diff --check follow the save. The original direct-source/no-project-map rationale remains.

## Independence provenance

Same concrete independent nonauthor reviewer task /root/independent_design_review. User supplied new concerns; reviewer independently checked current Design/Workflow, retained whole-package basis, source resource constraints and actual installer safety paths. Primary-agent authored the model contributions; reviewer has made no model or implementation edits. User findings are assessed as evidence, not assumed conclusions.
